request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 1:
A: The newly added Salesforce refresh block runs unconditionally inside connection setup — every time a jsforce.Connection is constructed the code fetches a fresh token from login.salesforce.com and writes it via prisma.credential.update, regardless of whether the existing access_token is expired. On any deployment with salesforce installed, each calendar operation that builds a service adds one outbound token request plus one credential DB write to the hot path, multiplying Salesforce API consumption and credential-row churn; token endpoint rate limits now gate ordinary calendar reads.
B: The Salesforce service constructor now unconditionally performs a remote POST to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update on every instantiation, whereas previously the connection was built from the stored token without any eager refresh or DB write. Every calendar operation that constructs the service (listing events, booking checks) now costs a network round-trip to Salesforce and a credential write even when the stored token is still valid; a transient Salesforce outage converts every read into an exception raised from object construction.

PAIR 6:
A: Both computed schema keys, [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], evaluate to the literal property name "[object Object]" (the second silently overwrites the first), so the "any number property is the expiry" catch-all described in the comment does not exist and z.object strips every real field except access_token. In sync mode no expiry field (expiry_date/expires_in) is ever validated or preserved: Office365 credentials keep their stale expired expiry_date and hit the parent sync endpoint on every calendar operation, and Zoom credentials lose expires_in entirely, forcing a refresh per call.
B: The minimumTokenResponseSchema catch-all keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (Object.prototype.toString on a Zod instance), so the schema is `{access_token, "[object Object]"}` and the intended 'any numeric property is the expiry' wildcard never matches; zod's default stripping then drops every field except access_token. In sync mode the parsed token response contains only access_token — expiry_date/expires_in and any other fields are silently stripped, so downstream expiry computations get undefined/NaN even once the Response-shape bug is fixed.
